issues.display_title: Issue #4129: Add delete (hide) action to Featured Photographers support list
issues.main_description_html:
Context

Support agents need a way to remove a photographer request from the GoThru Photographer request list on /support/featured-photographers without deleting the underlying request data or touching the photographer's GoThru account. The backend proxy is already available:

PATCH /photographers/support/delete-flag — body { "gothruUserId": number, "isDeleted": boolean } (super-user only).

Related API task: GoThruMedia/GoThru-API-New#1688

Scope

On /support/featured-photographers, add a delete action to each row in the action cell (currently Review and Login):

  • Icon-only button (fa-trash-can, danger / flat) with a "Delete Request" tooltip, placed to the left of Review.
  • Opens the existing DeleteModal (@pages/Photographer/Components/DeleteModal) for confirmation — the dashboard has no un-hide UI, so a mis-click can only be undone through the API. Copy: "{name} will be removed from the GoThru Photographer request list. The request data itself is kept and not deleted."
  • On confirm, call PATCH /photographers/support/delete-flag with { gothruUserId, isDeleted: true }.
  • On success: toast + refetch the list at the current page / limit / search / filter, so pagination totals stay correct.
  • On error: toast the API error (400 invalid id, 404 photographer not found, 403 non super-user).

Files

  • src/pages/Support/FeaturedPhotographers.jsx

Notes

  • Reuses usePatch (src/hooks/useRequest.jsx), NextUI Tooltip, and the existing DeleteModal — no new hook or component.
  • Modal title/description and the tooltip use plain English strings, matching the rest of this page, so no new i18n keys are added across the locale files.

Follow-up

  • Deleting the last row on the last page leaves an empty page; step the page back if it becomes a problem.
  • No un-hide (isDeleted: false) action in the dashboard yet.

issues.display_title: Issue #4135: About Form Mishandles the Logo on Save and Skips Validation
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

On /portfolio/settings/about, saving the form mishandles the logo in several ways:

  1. About.jsx only appends logo when a new file is picked. Clearing the upload sets fileLogo to '', which is falsy — so "logo removed" and "logo untouched" produce the same request body and the API cannot tell them apart.
  2. The upload placeholder promises "PNG only, max 10mb" but nothing enforces it. A JPG or an oversized file is only rejected by the API, as a bare 400 with no field-level message.
  3. fileLogo is never cleared after a successful save, so every later save re-uploads the same file and re-runs the progress bar.
  4. The progress bar under the preview keys off the form's loading flag, so it appears even on a save that uploads nothing.
  5. The remove button stays clickable while a save is in flight.
  6. Email is checked for emptiness only, so a malformed address is accepted and stored.

Expected behavior

  • Clearing the logo sends an explicit signal the API can act on; leaving it alone sends nothing.
  • A logo violating the PNG / 10mb rule is rejected in the browser, with a clear message, and the preview falls back to the stored logo.
  • The file dialog filters to .png up front.
  • A second save does not resend a logo that is already stored.
  • The progress bar only appears while a logo is actually uploading.
  • The remove button stays visible during a save but cannot be triggered.
  • Empty and malformed email show different messages.

Acceptance criteria

  • Removing the logo and saving clears it server-side.
  • Saving without touching the logo leaves it intact (needs the API fix).
  • A non-PNG or >10mb file is rejected before the upload starts, with a toast.
  • Saving twice in a row uploads the logo once; the second save shows no progress bar.
  • The remove button is visible but disabled while a save runs.
  • A malformed email blocks save and shows "Please enter a valid email address."
  • Both new strings are translated in all 18 locales.

Related

  • API issue: GoThruMedia/GoThru-API-New#1696 — the API wipes the logo on every save; that fix must merge first or the remove button stays inert.
  • PR: #4134

Dev update — 2026-07-22

PR #4134 (base development), branch fix/portfolio-logo-overwrite, 3 commits.

  • Settings/validation.js (new) — isValidLogoFile + EMAIL_REGEX, mirroring the API's logo => file|max:10000|mimes:png. Kept out of DetailInfo.jsx because importing that file pulls in @components → Particle.jsx → @tsparticles/react, ESM that jest cannot transform.
  • About.jsx — fileLogo is three-state (File / '' removed / null untouched); '' sends remove_logo=1. onCompleted resets it and the progress so a second save sends nothing; onError leaves it for a retry. A rejected logo raises a toast and is dropped via failedUpload.
  • SingleUpload.jsx — new accept prop (default unchanged, other 5 call sites untouched); the bottom-positioned remove button now honours isLoadingDelete and is a real <button>, so disabled works.
  • 18 locales — t_logo_invalid, t_email.t_error_message_invalid.
  • Settings/validation.test.js — 4 tests passing, eslint clean.

issues.display_title: Issue #4083: Implement Clarify Free AI Tokens Conversion in AI Blur Modal
issues.main_description_html:
Description

A UX issue was reported where users (specifically new users) can successfully apply AI Blur even when their account appears to have 0 standard tokens. The system grants free AI tokens, but that balance is hidden, and the Order Summary modal silently folds it into the deduction — showing a confusing "Total Cost: 0 Tokens" with no indication of which tokens (free vs. paid) were consumed.

This task makes the Free AI Token balance visible and breaks the deduction down so the billing math is clear.

📐 Based on approved design: docs/brains/2026-06-17-ai-blur-free-token-balance-design.md (Status: Approved).
⚠️ Note: The design sets the conversion as 1 paid Token = 10 AI Tokens (the original ticket said "20"). The design value is authoritative.

Affected File

  • src/pages/Tour/Detail/Blur/Components/AIBlurModal.jsx

The API already returns v1CreditData.free_trial (the free AI token balance), but it is currently folded into effectiveCreditAvailable without being surfaced to the user.

Design Overview

New computed values (added after savedForLater, ~line 91)

  • freeCreditsAvailable — free AI tokens from v1CreditData.free_trial (only for isAllowedUser; else 0).
  • freeCreditsApplied — min(freeCreditsAvailable, blurringCost).
  • paidCreditsApplied — paid subscription credits consumed after free credits run out.

No changes to existing values (blurringCost, effectiveCreditAvailable, totalCost, tokenRequired, savedForLater).

Order Summary UI changes

  1. New "Free AI Tokens" balance row (only when isAllowedUser), inserted before the Blurring Cost row:
    • Chip is green with a gift icon (fa-gift) when freeCreditsAvailable > 0.
    • Chip is muted grey with a ban icon (fa-ban) when freeCreditsAvailable === 0.
    • ℹ️ tooltip text: "Free AI Tokens are given at no cost and are used first before your paid Tokens. 1 paid Token = 10 AI Tokens."
  2. Replace the "Available AI Tokens Used" row with conditional indented sub-rows for allowed users:
    • "Free Tokens Applied" (green, fa-gift) when freeCreditsApplied > 0.
    • "Paid Credits Applied" (amber, fa-coins) when paidCreditsApplied > 0.
    • Non-allowed users keep the original single row unchanged.

Behavior by scenario

Scenario Free AI Tokens chip Sub-rows shown
1 — All free (free covers full cost) 🟢 green, balance > 0 "Free Tokens Applied" only
2 — Mixed (free exhausted, subscription fills rest) 🟢 green, balance > 0 "Free Tokens Applied" → "Paid Credits Applied"
3 — No free (0 free tokens) ⬜ muted grey, balance = 0 Neither sub-row shown

i18n

Add four keys under t_panorama_tools.t_ai_blur.t_modal to all 18 locale files (ba, cs, da, de, en, es, fr, hi, it, jp, nl, pl, pt, ro, ru, sk, sv, zh); en.json is authoritative, others receive the English string until translated:

  • t_free_tokens_available → "Free AI Tokens"
  • t_free_tokens_available_tooltip → "Free AI Tokens are given at no cost and are used first before your paid Tokens. 1 paid Token = 10 AI Tokens."
  • t_free_tokens_applied → "Free Tokens Applied"
  • t_paid_credits_applied → "Paid Credits Applied"

Acceptance Criteria

  1. When isAllowedUser is true, a "Free AI Tokens" row appears above "Blurring Cost" in the order summary.
  2. When freeCreditsAvailable > 0, the chip is green with a gift icon (fa-gift).
  3. When freeCreditsAvailable === 0, the chip is muted grey with a ban icon (fa-ban).
  4. The ℹ️ tooltip reads: "Free AI Tokens are given at no cost and are used first before your paid Tokens. 1 paid Token = 10 AI Tokens."
  5. When free credits cover the full cost: only the "Free Tokens Applied" sub-row appears (green, indented).
  6. When cost exceeds the free balance and subscription credits fill the rest: both "Free Tokens Applied" (green) and "Paid Credits Applied" (amber) sub-rows appear.
  7. When freeCreditsAvailable === 0: neither sub-row appears.
  8. Non-allowed users see the original "Available AI Tokens Used" row unchanged.
  9. All 18 locale files have the four new i18n keys added.
  10. Dark mode is supported for all new elements (green/amber tonal variants).

Out of Scope

  • Changing how tokens are consumed or the order of credit deduction.
  • Showing the free token balance anywhere outside this modal.
  • Translating the four new keys into non-English locales.
  • Changes to isNoToken / isHasToken / isUnsubscribe state logic.

Reference: docs/brains/2026-06-17-ai-blur-free-token-balance-design.md (approved design) and docs/superpowers/specs/analyze-all.md §5.2 (Token micropayments). Related to blur work #4072–#4075.

issues.display_title: Issue #4157: AI Blur Modal — Order Summary redesign + Blur Method (save_only)
issues.main_description_html:
Context

The AI Blur modal's Order Summary hid two steps users needed to see: the credit deduction and the rounding up to whole tokens. Numbers "jumped" (e.g. Blurring Cost 20 → Total Cost 5) with no explanation, and two look-alike units ("AI Token" vs "Token") read as a typo. This task clarifies the summary and adds a Blur Method choice wired to the new API save_only flag.

Changes

1. Order Summary clarity

  • Token rate fixed at 1 Token = 20 AI Tokens (CREDITS_PER_TOKEN = 20).
  • Added Credit Applied −N AI Tokens row so the drop from Blurring Cost to Total Cost is explained.
  • Added N AI Tokens saved for later note explaining the round-up to whole tokens.
  • Removed the ambiguous "worth" sub-line; moved the token-rate hint below the summary.
  • Modal widened md → lg.

2. Blur Method (gated)

  • New exclusive picker: Auto Blur (detect + blur immediately, permanent) and Save Blur (detect + save selection, review before publishing).
  • Default: Auto Blur.
  • Visible to allowed users only (useAllowedUser). Non-allowed users don't see the picker and stay on the Auto default.

3. API integration (save_only)

  • POST /tours/ai-blur now sends save_only: Save Blur → true (persist only, not published), Auto Blur → false (unchanged behavior).

4. Processing feedback

  • usePanoramas now exposes overallStatus from the processing SSE.
  • Blur page refetches manual-blur data (blurPanoIds) on each overallStatus === 'DONE' transition, so blur indicators reflect the just-blurred panos.

5. i18n

  • Modal wired through useCustomTranslate.
  • New keys across all 18 locales: t_blur_method, t_mode_auto(_desc), t_mode_save(_desc), t_token_rate_note, t_cost_per_image_tooltip, t_credit_applied, t_saved_for_later_note.

Acceptance criteria

  • Order Summary shows Blurring Cost, Credit Applied (when credits > 0), Total Cost, and Tokens with the saved-for-later note.
  • Token math: tokenRequired = ceil(totalCost / 20); Blurring − Credit = Total; Token×20 − Total = saved-for-later.
  • Blur Method picker shows for allowed users only; toggles Auto/Save, never empty, default Auto.
  • Non-allowed users: no picker, request sends save_only: false.
  • Save Blur sends save_only: true; Auto sends false.
  • All modal copy resolves via i18n in every locale (no raw keys shown).
  • Unsubscribe / Buy Token / Apply states unchanged.

These remaining credits come from the previous blur process. The formula is as follows:
1 Token (GoThru Token) => 20 AI Tokens (Credits), and 1 AI Token for 1 Panorama.
If a user processes 15 Panoramas, there will be 5 unused credits remaining, which will be used in the next blur process.

issues.display_title: Issue #4160: Portfolio: guide photographers to submit Street View panorama (not place) links
issues.main_description_html:
Context

On /photographer/portfolio, the Google Street View Portfolio section accepts a Google Maps share link. All share links look identical (maps.app.goo.gl/...) but resolve to different targets — place, panorama, coordinates, directions. The portfolio needs the panorama asset; a place link silently fails.

issues.main_description_html:
2026-07-27.13-14-44.mp4

Problem

Downgrading from the Subscription Status popup (SideMenu) opens the payment modal, but there is no way to pay. The plan name and price show on the left, and the payment side is blank — no card form, no PayPal button, and no confirm button. The user cannot complete the downgrade.

The same thing happens in the "downgrade to Basic" offer shown during unsubscribe.

Downgrading from /profile/subscription works normally.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Log in with an account on Pro, Pro Yearly, or Agency with an active recurring subscription.
  2. Open the SideMenu → Subscription Status.
  3. Click Downgrade.
  4. The payment modal opens. Plan and price are correct, but the payment section is empty and there is no confirm button.

Second path: SideMenu → Subscription Status → Unsubscribe → take the "downgrade to Basic" offer instead. Same result.

Expected

The same payment modal the user gets when downgrading from /profile/subscription, showing the payment method that matches how they subscribed (Stripe or PayPal).

Root cause

The popup opens the payment modal without telling it which subscription the user is currently on. The modal picks which payment method to show based on that information, so when nothing is passed it shows neither, and the confirm button is hidden along with them.

The subscription page passes those details; the popup and the unsubscribe flow do not.

  • Working reference: src/pages/Profile/Subscription/Subscription.jsx:476-487
  • Broken: src/components/organism/SideMenu/SubscriptionStatus.jsx:221
  • Broken: src/components/organism/PaymentV2/Unsubscribe.jsx:302

Only these two are affected. The other places that open the payment modal are one-time purchases (tokens, overlay unlocks), which do not go through this check.

Scope

  1. Pass the same subscription details the subscription page already passes — recurring profile, current subscription code, and the one-time-payment flag — at both SubscriptionStatus.jsx:221 and Unsubscribe.jsx:302.
  2. Re-test downgrade from both entry points, on a Stripe account and on a PayPal account.

Besides the blank payment section, the missing details also mean the user's current plan is not disabled in the monthly/yearly switcher inside the modal, and one-time-payment users see the recurring-payment notice. Both are fixed by the same change.

Notes

Two other problems in this popup's downgrade path are already recorded under "Notes" in #4164 and are not part of this issue: the Downgrade button doing nothing for some subscription codes, and the missing space add-on guard.

issues.display_title: Issue #4166: AI Blur Modal — move warning note between blur methods, agree checkbox to footer
issues.main_description_html:
Follow-up to #4162, which covers the same modal. This issue supersedes it with the final scope agreed with the client: the agreement checkbox moves into the modal footer rather than only shrinking the note, the work must be done with the UI-UX-PRO-MAX plugin, and the result needs PM / UI Designer sign-off before merge.

Component: src/pages/Tour/Detail/Blur/Components/AIBlurModal.jsx

Problem

The AI Blur modal body is a single space-y-4 stack: Blur Method → Order Summary → Token rate note → yellow warning note → agreement checkbox. With scrollBehavior="inside" the checkbox falls below the fold, so users have to scroll before they can enable Apply. The warning note also applies only to Auto Blur (the irreversible mode), but it is currently shown for both modes.

Sub-tasks (Frontend)

  • Relocate the warning note. Move the yellow warning block (info-box info-box--yellow, currently AIBlurModal.jsx:469-479) from the bottom of the modal to directly below the Auto Blur method row, i.e. between the Auto Blur and Save Blur options.
  • Conditional rendering. Show the warning note only while blurMode === 'auto'. It must disappear when the user selects Save Blur and reappear when they switch back. Note the method picker is gated behind useAllowedUser() — when the picker is hidden, the mode stays on the auto default, so the note must still render.
  • Shrink the warning text. Reduce the note's font size (currently text-small) and padding so the block reads as inline guidance for the selected method, not a page-level alert.
  • Move the agreement checkbox to the footer. Take the "I agree" checkbox (AIBlurModal.jsx:481-492) out of the scrolling body and put it in CustomModal's footerContent, on the left of the Cancel / Apply buttons. It must stay visible regardless of body scroll position, and keep driving isApplyDisabled. Footer needs to stay usable at size="lg" on narrow viewports — wrap or stack rather than overflow.
  • Verify both light and dark mode. The modal renders on dark:bg-zinc-700; keep using the app's zinc-* pairs, not NextUI semantic scales (they invert in dark mode).

Design process

  • Use the UI-UX-PRO-MAX plugin for the layout and spacing decisions (warning-note treatment, footer composition, type scale).
  • Present the result to PM / UI Designer for approval before merging. Attach before/after screenshots in light and dark mode to the PR.

Acceptance criteria

  1. The yellow warning note sits between the Auto Blur and Save Blur method rows.
  2. The note is visible when Auto Blur is selected and hidden when Save Blur is selected, updating on every switch.
  3. The note's text is visibly smaller than the current iteration.
  4. The agreement checkbox lives in the modal footer and is visible without scrolling, at every modal state (subscribed / no token / has token).
  5. Apply stays disabled until the checkbox is ticked, unchanged from current behaviour.
  6. Layout holds up in both light and dark mode, and on a short viewport.
  7. PM / UI Designer has approved the design before merge.

Out of scope

Order Summary content and the token arithmetic — unchanged from #4157.

useSpaceAddon.jsx:114-143 (handleSpaceAddon) calls POST /v2/payment/subscription/space-addon and only ever treats the response as success (onCompleted → handleSpaceAddonSuccess) or failure (onError → handleSpaceAddonError). There is no check for a 202/requires_action response.

useDowngradeOrUpgrade.jsx:288-361 (handleDowngradeOrUpgrade) already implements this for the upgrade flow:

  • checks plan?.action === 'UPGRADE' && res.data.status === 'requires_action'
  • builds a Stripe client via window.Stripe(...) (test/live key picked by isTestUserForPayment(userId))
  • calls stripeClient.confirmCardPayment(res.data.client_secret)
  • on result.paymentIntent.status === 'succeeded', posts { pi: res.data.client_secret } to a completion endpoint (complete3DsUpgrade, POST /v2/payment/subscription/complete-3ds-upgrade)
  • on completion success/error, calls the same handleDowngradeOrUpgradeSuccess/handleDowngradeOrUpgradeError the non-3DS path already uses

Because space-addon never checks for requires_action, a user whose card requires 3DS today just sees the generic buy-storage failure modal (handleSpaceAddonError) even though the card itself is fine.

Target state

handleSpaceAddon in useSpaceAddon.jsx follows the same branch handleDowngradeOrUpgrade uses:

  • if res.data.status === 'requires_action': run stripeClient.confirmCardPayment(res.data.client_secret), then on success POST { pi: res.data.client_secret } to POST /v2/payment/subscription/complete-space-addon-3ds (new hook, e.g. completeSpaceAddon3ds), then call the existing handleSpaceAddonSuccess/handleSpaceAddonError on that call's outcome
  • if result.error from confirmCardPayment: call handleSpaceAddonError
  • otherwise (no requires_action): unchanged, existing success/error handling

No new UI/modal needed — usePaymentStatus's existing showPaymentStatus({ type: 'success' | 'failed' }) (already used by both handleSpaceAddonSuccess and handleSpaceAddonError) covers both outcomes of the 3DS-completed flow too.

Scope

  • src/components/organism/PaymentV2/Hooks/useSpaceAddon.jsx
    • add [completeSpaceAddon3ds] = usePost({ url: '/v2/payment/subscription/complete-space-addon-3ds' })
    • handleSpaceAddon — branch on res.data.status === 'requires_action' inside the spaceAddon(...) onCompleted, matching useDowngradeOrUpgrade.jsx:305-346

Out of scope

  • useDowngradeOrUpgrade.jsx — already handles 3DS for upgrade, not touched.
  • SpaceAddOn.jsx (UI component) and PaymentV2.jsx — no prop/UI changes expected; handleSpaceAddon's external contract (the returned Promise) stays the same.
  • Any new modal component — reuse usePaymentStatus.

Risk / test plan

  • Manual QA in Stripe test mode: buy storage with a 3DS test card → confirm the 3DS challenge appears (Stripe.js handles this via confirmCardPayment), complete it, confirm the buy-storage success modal appears and storage is granted.
  • Manual QA: buy storage with a non-3DS test card → unchanged, completes without any 3DS prompt.
  • Manual QA: abandon/fail the 3DS challenge → confirm the buy-storage failure modal appears (via handleSpaceAddonError), not a silent hang.
